import pytest
from target import unescapeHTML

# Helper to assert that the output length matches expectation (no hidden changes)
def assert_length_unchanged(input_str, output_str):
    # For inputs without entities, length should be unchanged
    if '&' not in input_str or ';' not in input_str:
        assert len(output_str) == len(input_str)

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "inp,expected",
    [
        (None, None),
        ("", ""),
        ("Hello World", "Hello World"),
        ("Fish & Chips", "Fish & Chips"),
        ("&", "&"),
        ("<", "<"),
        (">", ">"),
        ("a < b & c", "a < b & c"),
        (""Hello"", '"Hello"'),
        ("'test'", "'test'"),
    ],
)
def test_unescape_basic_cases(inp, expected):
    assert unescapeHTML(inp) == expected
    if isinstance(inp, str):
        assert_length_unchanged(inp, unescapeHTML(inp))

def test_invalid_type_raises():
    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
        unescapeHTML(123)  # not a compat_str

def test_entity_like_with_extra_ampersand_is_unchanged():
    # Old implementation would not match because of the extra '&' inside the entity name
    # New implementation must preserve this behavior
    s = "&foo&bar;"
    assert unescapeHTML(s) == s

def test_multiple_consecutive_entities():
    s = "&<>"'"
    expected = "&<>\"'"
    assert unescapeHTML(s) == expected

def test_entity_without_semicolon_is_unchanged():
    s = "&amp without semicolon"
    assert unescapeHTML(s) == s

def test_entity_with_internal_semicolon_is_handled_correctly():
    # Only the first semicolon should terminate the entity
    s = "&foo;bar;"
    # Old regex stops at the first ';' after '&'
    # So only '&' is transformed, rest stays as is
    expected = "&foo;bar;"
    assert unescapeHTML(s) == expected

def test_long_string_performance_and_correctness():
    # Build a long string with many entities and normal text
    parts = ["&", "Hello", "<", "World", ">", "!", """, "Test", "'"]
    s = " ".join(parts * 100)  # repeat to increase size
    # Expected transformation using the same logic as old implementation
    expected = " ".join(
        ["&", "Hello", "<", "World", ">", "!", '"', "Test", "'"] * 100
    )
    assert unescapeHTML(s) == expected
